# `set_calib_param`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set the stored calibration frame count for a frame type.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (D64 and D32 command-socket invocation) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, set_calib_param @0xe6fe0, SetCalibrateParam @0x1936e0 |

Stores an integer per frame type (dark, bias or flat) and persists it to configuration. The meaning as a frame count is inferred. No range check on the value and no active-capture or mount gate. The configuration write result is ignored.

Side effects: Overwrites the stored per-type calibration integer and persists it in the imager stack settings. Every full call also makes the shared diagnostic log writes.

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_calib_param"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Object, or positional array [type, number]; extra elements ignored. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | type is not a string | `expected string param` |
| 104 | number missing or not an integer | `expected int param` |
| 209 | Unknown or light type (or type outside the dark/bias/flat range) | `invalid value` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

## Example

Request, set-dark - Set the dark count (shape per static analysis; value invented):

```json
{"id":45,"method":"set_calib_param","params":{"type":"dark","number":20}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_calib_param","result":0,"code":0,"id":45}
```

Reply, bad-number:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_calib_param","error":"expected int param","code":104,"id":46}
```
